Machine-consumption eligibility is unresolved corpus-wide pending AI governance.

Storage and repository topology (ADR-0003/ADR-0004 criteria apply when triggered).

capabilities.name: Institutional Method Library
capabilities.description: Governed internal corpus of Huerta Group methodology. The repository-based foundation is complete (the full approved Methodology Foundation v1 source, architecture, schema, registry, eight approved records, validation); substantive future methods remain blocked pending approved methodology substance (MFv1 §10.8).
unresolvedDecisions: Substantive future methods (assessments, diagnostics, implementation guidance, verification procedures) remain blocked pending approved methodology substance.
Disclosure tiers beyond internal, IP referral, and any future runtime application remain unresolved (ADR-0003/ADR-0004 criteria apply if triggered).
Final constitutional allocation of methodological approval authority (interim configurable Founder rule stands).

capabilities.name: Intellectual Property Repository
capabilities.description: Institutional IP Repository. The repository-based governance foundation is complete (the full approved Intellectual Property Foundation v1 source, architecture, schema, registry, six approved governance records, validation); no substantive asset is admitted, and all legally or commercially operative matters remain with Corporate Headquarters / legal authority.
unresolvedDecisions: Substantive asset admission is blocked: each future asset requires an approved source and a separate admission decision (none admitted; the six initial records are governance records).
All legally and commercially operative matters (ownership, protection, registration, licensing, valuation, commercialization) are reserved to Corporate Headquarters / legal authority.
Method Library referrals remain not_referred; future runtime capabilities (search, access control, database) require their own authorization (ADR-0003).
capabilities.notes: Repository foundation only — no runtime application, database, search service, portal, or administrative interface exists or is implied; no legal ownership or rights determinations are made.

capabilities.name: Education Platform
capabilities.description: Institutional Education Platform. Repository-based governance foundation complete (approved Education & Workforce Development Foundation v1, architecture, schema, registry, twelve governance records, validation); no program, learner, assessment, credential, offering, or LMS exists; learner data blocked by privacy/legal governance. Public /education page is positioning only.
unresolvedDecisions: No program, course, pathway, competency library, assessment instrument, credential, or offering exists or is approved: each requires separate Education-authority design, review, and approval (EWDFv1 §20.11, §21, §22.2).
Program approval never implies delivery readiness, enrollment availability, public disclosure, or commercial availability — the ten readiness dimensions remain separate (EWDFv1 §11.4–11.5, §12.2).

Any runtime education system (LMS, learner accounts, portals, dashboards, evidence submission) requires its own authorization under ADR-0003 criteria and ADR-0005 environment isolation; a generic LMS is explicitly not assumed appropriate, and no vendor, AI provider, or hosting model is selected (EWDFv1 §16.9, §19.3).

Production learner, instructor, assessment, organizational, and participation data remains blocked pending privacy and legal governance (EWDFv1 §14.5, §20.10); learner-record retention and disclosure await data-governance policy.

Credentialing, certification, continuing-education, instructor, learner-support, and commercial-model policy remain unresolved (EWDFv1 §20.12–20.14, §21); final constitutional allocation of educational approval authority is pending (interim configurable rule stands).
capabilities.notes: Repository foundation only — no LMS, runtime application, database, authentication, learner data, assessment operation, credential issuance, vendor selection, or public educational offering exists or is implied; repository presence creates no educational approval, and educational approval authorizes no delivery.

capabilities.name: Publishing Platform
capabilities.description: Publishing capability of Huerta Group LLC, implemented and operated by Huerta Group Publishing — the first chartered venture (FD-V1; fd-0007) — in its own repository. Editorial development, deterministic production, and evidence-gated releases operate under chartered delegated authority; commercial activation, distribution, public launch, and legal matters remain reserved.
unresolvedDecisions: Commercial activation, billing, and pricing remain reserved (Corporate Headquarters readiness + Founder Office authorization; Charter §8, §11).

Venture official public launch awaits its own Founder Office determination (parent-platform representation is determined — FD-V4, fd-0009 — with linking gated on launch); general name-use policy awaits FD-V3.
Distribution (ONIX, retail, manufacturing) is out of venture scope; legally operative rights and ISBN matters remain Corporate Headquarters matters.
capabilities.notes: identityRequirement records the parent-architecture reading: no parent identity capability is required or granted. The venture authenticates its own authors and staff on venture-owned infrastructure (Charter §7.3, §13) — venture-internal identity, outside this registry's identity dimension.

capabilities.name: AI Platform
capabilities.description: Future controlled use of institutional knowledge by AI: governed retrieval, permissions, evaluation, traceability. Philosophy exists (Vision Foundation §8); governance and runtime do not.
unresolvedDecisions: AI governance (access policy, decision rights, evaluation standards, data protection) is an owner decision.
Machine-consumption eligibility of every governed document is unresolved (knowledge manifest).

capabilities.name: Operations Systems
capabilities.description: Internal operational capability owned by Corporate Operations & Command Management. In LOCAL / PRE-PRODUCTION authentic Founder use (fd-0015): constructed, validated, and operating on the Founder's machine with encrypted off-machine backup and rehearsed recovery. Runtime lives in the private huerta-group-operations repository (ADR-0008). Production launch is NOT AUTHORIZED.
unresolvedDecisions: RECONCILED (fd-0014): implementationReadiness moved from governance_blocked to ready_with_owner_authorization, and maturity from conceptual to standby — the posture the notification service already established here: implemented and validated, deliberately not activated, awaiting an owner decision. repositoryDisposition moved from unresolved to future_separate_repository per ADR-0008. HISTORICAL POSTURE, preserved and not rewritten: this entry previously recorded that technical architecture was authorized to resume, design only, and that implementation remained NOT AUTHORIZED. That was accurate for its period; the Founder Office construction authorization at fd-0014 is what changed it.

LOCAL / PRE-PRODUCTION AUTHENTIC USE (fd-0015): the Founder Office declined production expenditure and authorized authentic Founder use locally. maturity stays 'standby' rather than moving to 'operational' because the capability is not activated in production — local authentic use is expressly not deployment (fd-0015 §2.5) — and implementationReadiness stays 'ready_with_owner_authorization' because production still awaits owner authorization and cost approval. The architecture is UNCHANGED: the deferral is a capital-allocation decision, ADR-0009 remains controlling, and Generation One may not be placed inside the existing public Supabase project to stay within Free-tier limits.

OPEN — the production-cost question is deferred, not closed. It returns to the Founder Office when authentic use demonstrates that persistent hosted availability would materially improve operations, when local operation becomes materially limiting, or when another significant circumstance justifies reconsideration (fd-0015 §3).

FORMALLY DISPOSITIONED (fd-0014; Production Readiness phase): all four governance-classification mismatches are dispositioned rather than corrected, because each is a vocabulary gap and the Founder Office forbade both inventing controlled vocabulary and distorting implementation truth to fit stale vocabulary. architecturalDisposition, repositoryDisposition, identityRequirement and evidencePaths are therefore stale but not false, and the true position is stated in institution/governance/operations/generation-one-classification-mismatch-dispositions.md. identityRequirement is the sharpest: the enum has no 'required' value, so the registry understates the access posture of the only authenticated system the institution operates, and a schema amendment is RECOMMENDED. The fd-0014 determination remains controlling over the registry value in all four.

RESOLVED (Production Readiness phase): the runtime repository is durably preserved at huertagroupllc-git/huerta-group-operations, private, pushed and verified at parity. Backup and recovery are documented and a restore has been tested into an isolated Supabase project, 36 of 36 checks passing including that restored identities authenticate and that the restored register still refuses what the original refuses. HISTORICAL POSTURE, preserved: the runtime previously had no remote and no tested restore, and production readiness was blocked on both.

OPEN — production launch is NOT AUTHORIZED. The next gate is the Founder Office Generation One Construction & Validation Review. Successful pre-production validation is expressly not implicit production approval.

OPEN — Founder Office operational-policy questions, deferred by fd-0014 and not to be answered speculatively: the change horizon beyond Since Last Review; venture snapshot responsibility; the financial visibility boundary, to be determined with Accounting rather than inferred by Development; and the Administration & Compliance visibility boundary. Where one becomes necessary to determine actual Founder-facing behaviour, only the affected decision stops and the bounded question returns.

OPEN — no retention, deletion, archival or disclosure doctrine is implied by the ADR package or by the construction authorization (fd-0014 §6). Backup and recovery expectations must be documented before the store holds irreplaceable records (ADR-0009, ADR-0018); the pre-production store holds none.

RESOLVED (fd-0014, ADR-0020): the identity provider is selected — Supabase Auth on the project ADR-0009 already requires. No Founder Office return trigger fired: no accepted architecture changed, no significant new recurring cost, no consequential new external dependency.

RESOLVED (fd-0014): the recorded_at inclusion boundary for Since Last Review is determined, with occurred_at independently represented where known and never manufactured where unknown. Generation One operational-view doctrine only; no universal institutional temporal policy is established.

HISTORICAL POSTURE, preserved: the operations-systems trigger was determined FIRED by the Founder Office (fd-0011) after the Phase 1 reassessment (fd-0010) found a recurring workflow evidenced but the outgrowing limb not demonstrable on repository evidence alone. Earlier still, this entry recorded the trigger as 'the first recurring internal workflow that outgrows governed documents; none identified yet'.

HISTORICAL POSTURE, preserved: prospective operational doctrine did not exist when this entry was first written, and the reserved Foundation location stood empty. The Foundation is preserved at institution/foundations/operations/CORP-OPS-SEM-FND-V1.md (fd-0012, fd-0013) and the definition package that asked for it is closed. Foundation §§5–24 establish operational-instance semantics prospectively; they are not recovered OSPA, and no unavailable OSPA (S05–S08, S11–S15) may be inferred from them. The fd-0011 prohibition on inferring a transition model from S09 §9.28 stands.

HISTORICAL POSTURE, preserved: the complete Generation One Requirements Report had not reached the implementing office across two prior attempts (fd-0010 D2, fd-0011 D1, fd-0012 D2). It is preserved byte-identical at institution/governance/operations/GEN1-REQ-V1.md (fd-0013).

capabilities.name: Identity and Access
capabilities.description: Authentication/authorization for internal and client capabilities. First implemented for Generation One under ADR-0020 (Supabase Auth on that capability's own project), with row-level authorization as the enforcement layer. Technical user classes only — never institutional offices.
unresolvedDecisions: RESOLVED for Generation One (ADR-0020): the provider is Supabase Auth on Generation One's own project, selected against ADR-0006's criteria and decided on portability — the dependency is one JWT claim read inside row-level policies. HISTORICAL POSTURE, preserved: provider selection was deliberately open under ADR-0006, and this entry previously recorded that the triggering capability did not exist.

OPEN — shared-service topology. ADR-0006 requires identity be introduced as a shared service from the start, and ADR-0020 is compatible with that without settling it: whether a second consumer shares Generation One's project, receives its own, or federates is expressly a decision for that consumer's ADR, made when the consumer and its requirements exist. implementationReadiness stays requirements_incomplete because the incomplete requirements are the shared-service ones, not Generation One's.

OPEN — constitutional and institutional authority structures. Any mapping of institutional roles onto technical roles awaits that authority and is expressly out of scope (ADR-0006, ADR-0017, ADR-0020).

capabilities.name: Shared Data Services

unresolvedDecisions: Whether future systems share a Supabase project (schema-per-system) or use project-per-system is unresolved until the second data-owning system is authorized (ADR-0004 criteria).

unresolvedDecisions: Observability and incident response beyond platform logs await the first system whose sensitivity demands them (ADR-0005 triggers).
